title: From the Editor — Already Waiting
settingText: Hushwater: a weathered house at the edge of the road with winter damage still visible in repairs and pale wood. Through an open doorway, a small sealed packet rests on a plain table in the foreground. No readable label, no character reveal.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 12. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They already caught the magician.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina planted identities. Samuel planted expectations. Together they created encounters that looked impossible until somebody showed you the wires.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the impossible kept happening outside the trick.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they have traveled together long enough that nobody can have run ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No quiet conversations. No planted names. No careful setup.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Hushwater is waiting anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A house there has been holding something since winter for a man Brandon Mack has never been.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, everyone arrives at the mystery together.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

directionInline.text: This is an interior editorial/interstitial comic page, not a cover or dossier. Preserve the grounded Sunforge Outlaw visual world: hard Sunfields light, tactile dust, worn materials, ordinary frontier life, strong silhouettes and no generic cyberpunk.

The supplied lettering is exact production text. If a generation pass cannot render long body copy reliably, preserve the successful artwork with a clean reserved text field and correct the lettering separately rather than changing or shortening the copy.
No spoilers beyond what the supplied editorial text itself implies. Do not visually reveal the next issue's identity mistake, confrontation, culprit, resolution or other first-page surprise.

title: Hushwater
summary: The five travelers enter Hushwater together after weeks on the same road. No one could have gone ahead without the others knowing it.

panelPlan.text: Hushwater is a modest settlement of shaded homes around a communal dining court, with winter repairs visible in mismatched pale boards.
The five travelers arrive in one continuous group: Jessie driving, Brandon beside the rig, Eva, Raina and Samuel all visible together.
No obvious dark Sunforge structure dominates the immediate center; the place looks materially ordinary.
Maela Crow looks up from carrying folded cloth and fixes on Brandon with tired recognition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: All five of us arrived together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I was present for the drive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Keep the chronology obvious.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Please let me get water before chronology becomes a job.

title: Andrew Keane
summary: Maela recognizes Brandon as Andrew Keane with exhausted relief rather than theatrical shock, then goes inside before his correction can stop her.

panelPlan.text: Maela approaches slowly as if matching Brandon against a long-held mental image.
She addresses him as Andrew Keane and immediately turns toward her house, assuming recognition has completed a promise.
Brandon corrects her. Maela pauses but continues inside.
Raina and Samuel look at each other because neither has heard the name before.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: You are Andrew Keane.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm Brandon Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I've been waiting since winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That is a long time to wait for the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I have never heard that name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Neither have I.

title: The Packet
summary: Maela returns with a visibly old sealed cloth packet marked for ANDREW KEANE. The object's wear makes clear it was not prepared for the travelers' current arrival.

panelPlan.text: Maela returns carrying a faded cloth packet tied with an old seal. The exact scripted label ANDREW KEANE is legible on the packet.
The fabric shows worn folds, repaired stitching and dust darkening around the tied edge.
She places it on a table rather than directly in Brandon's hands.
Eva looks at Raina before looking at the packet, understanding that physical age now matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: This is why I was waiting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: His name is on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Your face is the one I was told to expect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: How long have you had the packet?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Longer than the person who told me you were coming.

title: Older Than the Story
summary: Raina examines the packet only with Maela's permission and finds mundane evidence of age: wear, old sealing material and repairs made before the recent travel season.

panelPlan.text: Maela allows Raina to inspect the outside without breaking the seal.
Raina notes faded fabric, old wax or resin at the tie, repeated handling wear and one repair in a thread no longer used in the settlement.
Jessie asks whether the packet itself could have been manufactured recently to look old.
Raina says it could be faked, but the simplest reading is that Maela has genuinely handled it for a long time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Could somebody age it on purpose?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Anything can be staged with enough work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you think this was?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I think the wear is consistent with months of ordinary handling. I want dates before conclusions.

title: Lysa
summary: Maela explains the packet began with her dying friend Lysa, who asked her to keep it for Andrew Keane before anyone ever described Brandon.

panelPlan.text: Maela sits across from Brandon with the packet between them and tells the story in practical sequence.
Lysa arrived sick the previous winter after months on the road and stayed in Maela's house.
Before she died, Lysa gave Maela the packet and asked her to keep it for Andrew Keane.
At that point Maela had no idea what Andrew looked like or whether he would ever come.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa gave it to me before she died.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Did she describe Andrew?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Not usefully. Dark hair. Taller than her. Younger than me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That could be half the Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Which is why I expected to die with the packet still in my house.

title: A Promise Without a Face
summary: For months Maela's promise had no face attached to it. She simply stored the packet and recorded it in her household ledger as an unresolved obligation.

panelPlan.text: Maela retrieves a thick household ledger used for food stores, visitors, repairs and debts.
An old winter entry records Lysa's stay, death and the packet for Andrew Keane among ordinary household facts.
Eva notices the entry predates everything they know about Brandon's current route.
Brandon does not touch the ledger or packet, leaving ownership with Maela.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I wrote it down because I was afraid I'd forget why I kept the thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The packet existed before anybody described Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Long before.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then whatever is inside belongs to a real Andrew, whether I resemble him or not.

title: The Traveler in Green
summary: Months later, a woman traveler with a green scarf and shaved left temple described a man matching Brandon closely enough that Maela connected him to Andrew.

panelPlan.text: Maela turns to a later ledger entry marking an overnight traveler.
She remembers a woman with a green scarf, dark hair shaved at the left temple and a repaired saddlebag.
The traveler asked about routes east, heard Maela mention the unresolved packet and said Andrew might be traveling under another name.
Samuel does not recognize the description and says so without overclaiming memory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Who connected the packet to Brandon's appearance?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: A woman passing through. Green scarf. Shaved on the left side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: That description means nothing to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: She knew enough about Andrew to make me listen.

title: The Way He Stands Near a Door
summary: The traveler's description was unusually specific: Brandon's coat, hair, build and habit of standing where he can see a door. Maela believed the promise finally had an endpoint.

panelPlan.text: Maela lists the description while Brandon happens to stand at the edge of the room with the door in peripheral view.
Jessie notices the behavioral match but also remembers similar details appeared in Raina's planted tests.
Eva asks whether the traveler ever saw the packet or read the name Andrew from it before offering the description.
Maela says the packet stayed inside; she mentioned the name during conversation first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Dark coat. Black hair to the shoulders. Lean. Watches doors without turning his whole head.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That is more specific than a face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did she see the packet first?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: No. I told her about Andrew because she was asking who passed through here.

title: Open It
summary: Maela asks Brandon to open the packet so her promise can finally end. Brandon refuses because resemblance and expectation do not make him the named recipient.

panelPlan.text: Maela pushes the packet halfway across the table toward Brandon.
Brandon keeps both hands away from it.
Maela says Lysa died believing Andrew would come and that she has carried the obligation through a year of ordinary life.
Brandon points to the scripted name ANDREW KEANE rather than arguing about his face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Open it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Because his name is on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa died believing he'd come.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then I would rather disappoint you than take his place.

title: The Ledger Date
summary: Raina turns from identity to chronology. Maela's ledger provides a date for the green-scarf traveler's visit, and that date falls months before Raina first heard Brandon's name.

panelPlan.text: Raina lays her dated field notebook beside Maela's household ledger.
The Hushwater traveler entry is marked in late winter.
Raina's earliest Brandon entry from the Brannock rumor is five months later.
Eva checks both dates herself before reacting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: This visit was five months before my first Brandon note.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Before you heard about the Last Drop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Before I knew Brandon Mack existed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Check it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I already did. I will do it a third time.

title: Before Samuel
summary: The date also predates Samuel joining Raina. Their admitted operation cannot have caused the Hushwater setup through the method exposed in Issue 4.

panelPlan.text: Samuel checks his own older travel notes and locates where he was during the winter entry.
He was traveling a distant route and had not yet met Raina.
Raina and Samuel compare timelines with none of their former defensive certainty.
Maela watches the investigators discover that their explanation does not reach far enough backward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I had not met Raina yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You could not have gotten Brandon's description from her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I could not have gotten Brandon's description from anybody. I did not know there was a Brandon to describe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Our operation cannot be the source of this visit.

title: Could the Story Have Doubled Back
summary: Jessie tests the remaining social explanation: perhaps a later Brandon story contaminated Maela's memory of an earlier traveler. Raina and Maela examine the written ledger for evidence of later editing.

panelPlan.text: Jessie proposes that Maela could have attached Brandon details to the old winter traveler after hearing later road stories.
Maela is offended for a moment, then accepts that memory can shift and points to the original written entry.
The entry contains brief physical notes about the green-scarf traveler and the phrase 'Andrew description,' but not Brandon's later name.
Raina notes consistent ink aging and page order without treating that as infallible forensic proof.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Could you have attached Brandon's details to an older memory after the road stories reached Hushwater?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I could remember badly. The ledger still exists.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: The entry was made in sequence with the winter accounts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The Last Drop story had not happened yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That route cannot carry information backward five months.

title: A Human Connection
summary: Raina keeps one human explanation alive: Brandon may have known Andrew Keane or the green-scarf traveler before any of them met him. The chronology defeats Raina's operation, not every possible human connection.

panelPlan.text: Outside Maela's house, Raina states the strongest ordinary hypothesis still available.
Brandon sits on a low wall mending a strap and does not react defensively to the idea that Andrew might be someone from his unknown-to-them past.
Eva and Jessie exchange a look shaped by months of traveling with him.
Samuel asks whether Brandon knows anyone matching the green-scarf description. Brandon says he does not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: There is still a human possibility. Brandon may have known Andrew or the woman who came here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know Andrew Keane.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Green scarf, shaved left temple?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Nobody I recognize.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That is not proof. It is only where the ordinary explanations still have room.

title: We Know Him Now
summary: Eva and Jessie no longer treat a false assigned identity as a live possibility every time evidence becomes strange. Their accumulated ordinary knowledge of Brandon changes the burden of proof.

panelPlan.text: Raina asks whether Eva and Jessie can truly exclude a hidden connection to Andrew given the years of Brandon's life they do not know.
Eva says she cannot exclude every past connection, but that is different from reopening the claim that Brandon secretly is Andrew.
Jessie says months of seeing Brandon make choices under pressure matters more to her than resemblance and rumor.
Brandon keeps working on the strap rather than validating either woman's faith in him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: You do not know every year of his life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That leaves room for people he knew. It does not make him Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We know him now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Knowing him now does not close the missing years.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It changes what I am willing to believe without evidence.

title: Brandon Is Enough
summary: The old central identity question becomes emotionally obsolete for Eva and Jessie. Brandon can still surprise them and have unknown history without becoming a hidden master identity.

panelPlan.text: Eva sits beside Brandon while Jessie checks the repaired strap.
Eva says she has stopped needing every blank in Brandon's past to contain another person.
Jessie states that Brandon is sufficient as the identity she travels with.
Samuel recognizes that the mystery has shifted away from confession and toward provenance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You can still surprise us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was hoping to avoid that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You can have a past without every stranger being right about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Brandon is enough for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Then Andrew becomes the interesting part.

title: Who Was Andrew
summary: The inquiry turns toward Andrew Keane rather than Brandon. Maela knows little beyond Lysa's confidence that Andrew would understand the packet and that he once traveled near the western salt route.

panelPlan.text: Samuel asks Maela what Lysa actually said about Andrew rather than what the later traveler supplied.
Maela remembers only fragments: western salt route, practical competence, a promise Lysa believed Andrew would understand.
Raina separates Lysa-derived facts from green-scarf-traveler-derived facts in her notes.
Eva sees how little remains once the layers are kept distinct.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: What did Lysa herself tell you about Andrew?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Western salt route. He fixed things. She trusted him with whatever is in the packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Nothing about a dark coat or how he stands near doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Those came from the traveler.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then we have two stories that met in this house.

title: I Wanted You To Be Him
summary: Maela admits the emotional force behind her certainty: she wanted Brandon to be Andrew because a correct recipient would release her from a promise she has carried since Lysa's death.

panelPlan.text: Maela holds the packet in both hands by the doorway while the others give her and Brandon space.
She says recognizing Brandon felt like relief before it felt like evidence.
Brandon does not criticize her for wanting the obligation to end.
Eva listens without turning Maela's grief into another test case.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I wanted you to be him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Then I could be finished with this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Wanting to be finished does not make you foolish.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: It made me certain faster than I should have been.

title: What the Promise Belongs To
summary: Brandon helps Maela separate two obligations: honoring Lysa's trust and deciding what to do when the intended recipient may never arrive. Pretending Brandon is Andrew would solve neither honestly.

panelPlan.text: Brandon sits across from Maela with the unopened packet still between them.
He says he cannot release her from Lysa's promise because he is not the person Lysa named.
He also says the promise cannot require Maela to wait forever without deciding what the obligation means now.
Samuel watches Brandon do work resembling pastoral care without taking over the conversation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So what am I supposed to do with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know, ma'am.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: The preacher would have something better.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I am trying very hard not to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I only know that giving it to the wrong man would not keep the promise.

title: Maela Decides
summary: Maela chooses to keep the packet sealed for now while changing the promise's terms in her own mind: she will continue asking after Andrew, but she will not force closure through any man who merely resembles him.

panelPlan.text: Maela reties the packet after checking the old knot, preserving the seal.
She writes a new ledger note beside the old entry: Brandon Mack arrived, not Andrew Keane.
The exact names are scripted readable text within the ledger only where required for the story beat.
She places the packet back in its ordinary storage drawer rather than on a shrine or special display.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I will keep it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That is your decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I dislike you a little for making me decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That seems fair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: You did better without my sermon.

title: Former Manipulators
summary: Raina and Samuel accept the changed status of their own explanation. Their operation was real and consequential, but Hushwater proves it was interference with a pattern rather than its origin.

panelPlan.text: At the communal dining court, Raina spreads only the essential timeline: Hushwater winter visit, Brannock months later, Samuel joining later still.
Samuel acknowledges that the methods they thought were creating controlled encounters may instead have been exploiting something already happening.
Jessie refuses to let the conclusion jump from 'not them' to any supernatural certainty.
Brandon points out that the green-scarf traveler remains a real human person they have not identified.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Our operation is demoted from cause to interference.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: We found a pattern and started pressing on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That still leaves a traveler in a green scarf, not a miracle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Find the person before you name the impossible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And if the person does not explain all of it, we keep going.

title: Who Is Brandon
summary: As they prepare to leave, Eva closes the notebook page that has been asking who Brandon really is. The answer she has is not a secret identity but accumulated lived knowledge.

panelPlan.text: Eva sits on the rig step with her cheap notebook open to an old page headed WHO IS BRANDON?
Below it are crossed or annotated names accumulated across the season.
She draws one clean line through the old question rather than through Brandon's actual name.
Brandon notices but does not ask to read over her shoulder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I know who you are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Enough to stop asking?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I am done trying to rename you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That should save paper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I have another question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Of course you do.

title: The Question Moves
summary: The five leave Hushwater together. Eva opens a new notebook page with the larger question: why do strangers and stories keep arriving before Brandon. The season closes the identity fakeout without closing the series mystery.

panelPlan.text: Maela remains at her doorway as the travelers leave, the packet safely out of sight inside.
Raina and Samuel travel beside the rig rather than ahead or behind, visually established as fellow witnesses now.
Eva writes a new question in her notebook while the road opens into immense Sunfields distance.
Final panel: far on a remote ridge, an unreadable rider silhouette may or may not be the same Rider seen before. No glow, impossible anatomy or supernatural effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Then what are you chasing now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why do strangers keep expecting someone with Brandon's face before we arrive?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: That is a larger question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Try not to make it larger than the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The road is already large enough.

title: Sunforge Outlaw Will Return
settingText: An immense western Sunfields road vanishing into luminous distance. Tiny travelers move forward while, on a remote ridge far off the road, a single unreadable rider silhouette may or may not be the same figure seen before. No supernatural effects.
summary: Art-directed season-closing editorial splash. Close the first twelve-issue movement while propelling the larger mystery forward without resolving it.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The easy mystery is over.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon Mack is still Brandon Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The road ahead is not getting simpler.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somewhere beyond Hushwater are towns they have never seen, people with stories that should not be there yet, and a Rider who has already taught them not to trust distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know more now.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Enough to know the first answer was only interference.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The road has stopped asking who Brandon is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The next question is bigger.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Sunfields are still ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And something keeps arriving first.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SUNFORGE OUTLAW WILL RETURN.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines
